passage:
A museum displayed a damaged helmet from a war. It was not polished. A crack ran across one side.
The guide said the museum kept it that way because the damage told part of the story. War should not be made to look clean.
Students stood quietly. The helmet had once belonged to a person, not a character in a game.
The teacher asked them to write one sentence about the object. One student wrote, "This is what danger looks like after it becomes silent."
The helmet taught more than dates. It reminded students that history's large events happen to individual bodies.
